clue.text: Bad blood shown by heartless opponent about it

indicators.note: a thing without its heart has lost its central letter, so the middle of the word goes
to be about something is to surround it, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: an opponent is an enemy
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ill feeling displayed by a callous rival over some matter.
explanation.walkthrough: The opponent's heart is its single middle letter; what remains then wraps around the short word 'it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad blood is an idiom for lasting hostility between people, which is exactly what enmity means.

clue.text: For example, loses one's composure after last of strong drinks

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter only

blocks.note: e.g. is the abbreviation for for example
the final letter of the word
to flip is to lose one's temper

explanation.surface: Someone goes to pieces after a few strong drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strong drinks' reads as one phrase, but 'strong' only lends its last letter and 'drinks' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Egg flips are drinks of beaten egg mixed with ale, spirits or milk, also called eggnog.

clue.text: Clergyman, old fellow, to tell government member

blocks.note: a minister is a member of the clergy
O is the abbreviation for old
F is the abbreviation for fellow
to state is to tell

explanation.surface: A priest and an old colleague brief a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clergyman' looks like the whole religious minister, but here it is only the first word of a government title.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister of state is a UK government minister ranking below a secretary of state, so a member of the government.

clue.text: Organised tour taking in centre of early market town

indicators.note: organised means put into a new order, so the letters are rearranged
the centre of a word is its middle letter
to take something in is to hold it inside

blocks.note: the letters of the word, to be rearranged
the third of five letters

explanation.surface: A guided trip arrives at a market town early in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: TOUR is rearranged as TURO, and R goes in after the T. Truro is the cathedral city of Cornwall, in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Truro is a Cornish town that grew up around its market, so it is an example of a market town.

clue.text: Smart to disconnect after energy conserved by family

indicators.note: what is conserved by something is kept safe inside it, so one piece sits within the other
after places the first-named piece behind the later one, so the clue's order is swapped in the grid

blocks.note: a clan is an extended family
E is the physics symbol for energy
to cut a line is to disconnect it

explanation.surface: A smart person cuts off the supply once the household has saved some power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' reads as the start of the instruction, but it is the definition, and 'to disconnect' is wordplay that ends up last.
explanation.definitionFit: Clean-cut describes a neat, well-groomed appearance, a near synonym of smart.

clue.text: Feature of spectacular Christmas tree

indicators.note: a feature of something is a part of it, so the answer is a part of the words that follow

blocks.note: the end of the first word joined to the start of the second

explanation.surface: A dazzling Christmas tree is the centrepiece of a display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Christmas tree' suggests a fir, but 'tree' is the definition on its own and the answer is a different conifer.
explanation.definitionFit: The larch is a deciduous conifer, so it is a kind of tree.

clue.text: Bird in brass - a lot manufactured

indicators.note: something manufactured is made from raw material, so the letters are made into a new word

blocks.note: all nine letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Plenty of bird ornaments are made out of brass.
explanation.definitionFit: The albatross is a large seabird with a very long wingspan.

clue.text: Cornelius is cool about opposing philosophies leading to conflict

indicators.note: about can mean turned around or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: all fifteen letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Cornelius stays calm about clashing worldviews heading for a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cool' and 'about' read as Cornelius keeping calm on a topic, but 'about' is the signal and 'is' belongs to the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Two sides on a collision course hold policies or views bound to clash, so the phrase names a path towards conflict.

clue.text: Aim at goal

blocks.note: first meaning: a verb, to direct something towards
second meaning: a noun, the thing one sets out to achieve

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a footballer's instruction to shoot at goal; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for directing efforts or weapons at something and a noun for an objective.

clue.text: Telephone system popular company installed in Trinity, for example

indicators.note: what is installed in something is fitted inside it

blocks.note: what is in is popular
Trinity is the summer term at Oxford and some other universities
Co. is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A successful firm fits a phone network into Trinity College.
explanation.walkthrough: Trinity suggests a Cambridge college, but it is also the name of the summer term at Oxford and Dublin.
explanation.definitionFit: An intercom is an internal telephone or speaker system linking rooms within a building.

clue.text: Arms race participant?

blocks.note: surface reading: a nation competing to build up weapons faster than its rivals
setter's reading: someone who races, or smuggles, weapons across borders illegally

explanation.surface: A country locked in a military build-up against its rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: The arms race is a Cold War phrase, but here the 'race' is a run: the person runs guns, smuggling weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunrunner smuggles firearms, so in a playful sense they take part in a race involving arms.

clue.text: Agricultural machine the Parisian kept in farm building, briefly

indicators.note: something said briefly is cut short, so the word loses its final letter
what is kept in a place is held inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a barn is a farm building
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: A French farmer's machine is stored in a barn.
explanation.walkthrough: BARN shortened to BAR holds LE: BA-LE-R.
explanation.definitionFit: A baler is a farm machine that compresses hay or straw into bales.

clue.text: Graceful Ragdoll is so meek inside

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the run of words just before it, straddling their word breaks

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of Ragdoll through is and so into the start of meek

explanation.surface: A Ragdoll cat is elegant and gentle by nature.
explanation.walkthrough: A Ragdoll is a breed of placid cat, which makes the surface about a docile pet.
explanation.definitionFit: Lissome means supple and slender in movement, a close synonym of graceful.

clue.text: Special phone link may cause heated row

blocks.note: heated means hot
a row is a line

explanation.surface: A dedicated phone connection can lead to an angry argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as a quarrel next to 'heated', but it is a line, as in a row of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotline is a direct telephone connection set up for a specific purpose, such as between heads of state.

clue.text: I consume poison - terrible illness results

indicators.note: something terrible is in a dreadful state, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: all fourteen letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Someone swallows poison and falls dreadfully sick.
explanation.definitionFit: Pneumoconiosis is a lung disease caused by inhaling dust, as miners do, so it is an illness.

clue.text: Joker, male, is seen on Baghdad river

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for male
taken as written
the Tigris is the river flowing through Baghdad

explanation.surface: A comedian is spotted on the river in Baghdad.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' puts the river below M and IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistigris is the joker or blank card used as a wild card in some games of poker.

clue.text: Canine with us, barking - a pest

indicators.note: barking is slang for mad, and mad letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: Canine and us, every letter

explanation.surface: A dog that lives with us keeps barking and drives us mad.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking fits the dog, but in British slang 'barking' (mad) is a common anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuisance is an annoying person or thing, which is what a pest means figuratively.

clue.text: Leader to go ashore in cape

blocks.note: a head is a leader
to land is to come ashore

explanation.surface: A captain disembarks wearing a cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cape' looks like a garment, but it is the headland sense, a point of land jutting into the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A headland is a narrow piece of high land projecting into the sea, the geographical sense of cape.

clue.text: Complaint in sheikdom, unease spreading

indicators.note: unease that is spreading moves about and changes shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: every letter of the two words

explanation.surface: Grievances spread through an Arab state as anxiety grows.
explanation.definitionFit: Housemaid's knee is an inflammation of the kneecap's bursa from kneeling, a medical complaint.

clue.text: I, about to step over frozen summit

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means turned over, so the word reads upwards

blocks.note: taken as written
c. is short for circa, Latin for about
a pace is a step

explanation.surface: A climber announces they are about to take a step across an icy peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'on the point of', but 'about' is C and 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An icecap is a permanent covering of ice, as on a mountain top or polar region.

clue.text: Dismiss teller

blocks.note: first meaning: to expel an officer from the armed forces in disgrace
second meaning: a person who handles money at a bank counter

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an order to sack a bank worker; the verb sense of the answer is military discharge.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to discharge in disgrace, and as a noun it names a bank clerk who pays out money.

clue.text: Heading off, yellow and black bird

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, and off means it is removed

blocks.note: yellow means cowardly, and craven means the same

explanation.surface: A yellow-and-black bird takes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yellow and black bird' looks like one colour description, but yellow is the wordplay and 'black bird' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The raven is a large all-black member of the crow family.

clue.text: Robot in Dr No novel brought in to help

indicators.note: novel means new or fresh, so the letters are made into a new order
something brought in to another thing is placed inside it

blocks.note: aid is help
the letters of the name, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A robot features in the James Bond novel Dr No as an assistant.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr No is a Bond novel, which makes 'novel' look like a description rather than the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An android is a robot made to look and act like a human.

clue.text: Dove flying over northern county

indicators.note: a bird flying is moving about freely, so the letters change places

blocks.note: the letters of the word, to be rearranged
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: A dove flies over a county in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the rearranged bird above N. Devon is a county in south-west England, which makes 'northern' a nice decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Devon is one of the English counties, in the south-west peninsula.

clue.text: I must sit in cleaner seat

indicators.note: to sit in something is to be placed inside it

blocks.note: a char, or charwoman, is a cleaner
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone insists on taking the cleaner's chair.
explanation.walkthrough: A char is an old British word for a woman paid to clean a house.
explanation.definitionFit: A chair is a seat for one person, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Smart having line deleted in travel document? The other way round

indicators.note: deleted means removed, and line is the conventional L, so that letter goes
what is in something is placed inside it

blocks.note: smart means clever
a visa is a travel document

explanation.surface: An elegant visa that has had a line struck out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: Line is the conventional L; the shortened word then sits inside the travel document, splitting it after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Vice versa is a Latin phrase meaning with the order or relation reversed.

clue.text: At Naples? That may be nice

indicators.note: the letters may be turned into something else, so they are recast into a new word

blocks.note: all eight letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A holiday in the Italian city of Naples would be agreeable.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasant means agreeable or enjoyable, a direct synonym of nice.

clue.text: Popular act? Certainly

blocks.note: what is in is fashionable or popular
a deed is an act

explanation.surface: Asked whether a stage act is a hit, someone answers yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Indeed is an emphatic word of agreement, used much as certainly is.
